formulas.title: Thermodynamic Stall Force of a Molecular Motor
formulas.description: Gives the maximum opposing load force $F_{\mathrm{stall}}$ that a tightly coupled molecular motor can sustain before its mean forward velocity drops to zero, equal to the chemical free energy per cycle $\Delta \mu$ divided by the step length $\delta$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The stall force is the thermodynamic upper bound on mechanical force generation where the mechanical work performed per step exactly equals the chemical free energy liberated by one fuel molecule.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A motor stalls when pushing its cargo one step forward costs every bit of energy available from burning a single ATP molecule.
formulas.interpretation: Obtained directly by setting $k_+ = k_-$ in the local detailed-balance stepping ratio $\exp[(\Delta \mu - F_{\mathrm{load}}\delta)/(k_B T)] = 1$. For kinesin with $\Delta \mu \approx 20\,k_B T \approx 83\,\mathrm{pN\cdot nm}$ and $\delta = 8\,\mathrm{nm}$, $F_{\mathrm{stall}} \le 10\,\mathrm{pN}$, consistent with measured optical-trap stall forces near $6\text{--}8\,\mathrm{pN}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Reflects energy conservation at the reversible quasistatic equilibrium point where net entropy production vanishes.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Represents an exact equality for tightly coupled motors and an upper bound ($F_{\mathrm{stall}} \le \Delta \mu / \delta$) whenever futile ATP hydrolysis or mechanical back-slippage pathways exist.

F_{\\mathrm{stall}}.name: Thermodynamic Stall Force
F_{\\mathrm{stall}}.description: Opposing load force at which the average motor drift velocity vanishes.

\\Delta \\mu.name: Chemical Free Energy per Cycle
\\Delta \\mu.description: Gibbs free-energy drop from hydrolyzing one fuel molecule (such as ATP).

\\delta.name: Motor Step Length
\\delta.description: Periodic distance traversed along the track per mechanochemical cycle.

formulas.title: Thermodynamic Mechanical Efficiency of a Molecular Motor
formulas.description: Defines the isothermal mechanical efficiency $\eta_{\mathrm{mech}}$ of a molecular motor as the ratio of useful mechanical output power $F_{\mathrm{load}} v$ delivered against an external load to the chemical input power $r_{\mathrm{ATP}} \Delta \mu$ supplied by ATP hydrolysis.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Unlike heat engines bounded by Carnot efficiency, isothermal molecular motors convert chemical free energy directly into mechanical work at constant temperature, allowing efficiency to approach unity in the reversible tight-coupling limit.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Mechanical efficiency measures what fraction of the chemical power burned from ATP goes into lifting or pulling an external load rather than warming the surrounding fluid.
formulas.interpretation: Because $v = (k_+ - k_-)\delta$ and for tight coupling $r_{\mathrm{ATP}} = k_+ - k_-$, the efficiency simplifies to $\eta_{\mathrm{mech}} = F_{\mathrm{load}} \delta / \Delta \mu = F_{\mathrm{load}} / F_{\mathrm{stall}}$, approaching $1$ as $F_{\mathrm{load}} \to F_{\mathrm{stall}}$ while output power vanishes.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from the first and second laws of isothermal nonequilibrium thermodynamics, requiring $\dot{W}_{\mathrm{out}} \le -\dot{G}_{\mathrm{chem}}$ so that $\eta_{\mathrm{mech}} \le 1$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Vanishes at zero load ($F_{\mathrm{load}} = 0$) and at stall ($v = 0$); for unloaded cargo transport against fluid drag alone, the complementary Stokes efficiency $\eta_S = \gamma v^2 / (r_{\mathrm{ATP}} \Delta \mu)$ is used instead.

\\eta_{\\mathrm{mech}}.name: Mechanical Efficiency
\\eta_{\\mathrm{mech}}.description: Dimensionless ratio of mechanical work rate to chemical free-energy consumption rate.

F_{\\mathrm{load}}.name: Opposing External Load Force
F_{\\mathrm{load}}.description: Constant force against which the motor performs useful mechanical work.

v.name: Mean Drift Velocity
v.description: Steady-state average forward velocity of the molecular motor.

r_{\\mathrm{ATP}}.name: Net ATP Hydrolysis Rate
r_{\\mathrm{ATP}}.description: Mean number of ATP molecules hydrolyzed per unit time during steady operation.

\\Delta \\mu.name: Chemical Free Energy of Hydrolysis
\\Delta \\mu.description: Gibbs free energy released per hydrolyzed ATP molecule.

formulas.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation (TUR)
formulas.description: Establishes a universal lower bound on the relative variance $\mathrm{Var}(X)/\langle X \rangle^2$ of any time-integrated nonequilibrium current $X$ in a steady-state Markovian system in terms of the total entropy production $\Sigma$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Precision in nanoscale transport has an irreducible thermodynamic price: suppressing relative fluctuations of a molecular motor's displacement or biochemical clock requires dissipating at least $2 k_B$ of entropy per unit inverse squared relative error.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A microscopic motor cannot be both ultra-steady and ultra-frugal; cutting its stepping jitter in half forces it to burn at least four times as much free energy into heat.
formulas.interpretation: Proved by Barato and Seifert (2015) and Gingrich et al. (2016) using large-deviation bounds on Markov jump processes and overdamped Langevin dynamics. Allows experimental inference of hidden entropy production $\Sigma \ge 2 k_B \langle X \rangle^2 / \mathrm{Var}(X)$ directly from observable motor trajectory statistics.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Originates from the convexity of the large-deviation rate function constrained by microscopic time-reversal symmetry and local detailed balance.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Holds for continuous-time Markov jump processes and overdamped Langevin systems in nonequilibrium steady states with time-independent driving. Can be violated by discrete-time chains, underdamped inertial dynamics, or time-periodic driving without generalized bounds.

\\mathrm{Var}(X).name: Current Variance
\\mathrm{Var}(X).description: Statistical variance $\langle X^2 \rangle - \langle X \rangle^2$ of the integrated current $X$ (dimensionless ratio with $\langle X \rangle^2$).

\\langle X \\rangle.name: Mean Integrated Current
\\langle X \\rangle.description: Ensemble average of any time-antisymmetric integrated current such as motor steps or hydrolyzed ATP count.

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Fundamental entropy scale relating dimensionless information to thermodynamic entropy.

\\Sigma.name: Total Entropy Production
\\Sigma.description: Total thermodynamic entropy generated in the system and heat bath during the observation interval.

formulas.title: Péclet Number for Drift-Versus-Diffusion Transport
formulas.description: Quantifies the dimensionless ratio of diffusive timescale $L^2 / D$ to advective drift timescale $L / v$ for a molecular motor or Brownian ratchet moving with mean velocity $v$ and effective diffusivity $D$ across a characteristic distance $L$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Péclet number measures whether directed active transport or random thermal diffusion dominates particle displacement over a given spatial length scale $L$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A large Péclet number means the motor marches reliably to its destination faster than random thermal wandering could carry it; a small value means thermal diffusion wins.
formulas.interpretation: For a kinesin motor ($v \approx 1\,\mu\mathrm{m/s}$, $D \approx 0.005\,\mu\mathrm{m}^2/\mathrm{s}$) traversing a $L = 10\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ axon segment, $\mathrm{Pe} \approx 2000 \gg 1$, explaining why eukaryotic cells require active molecular motors rather than passive diffusion for long-range transport.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Emerges from nondimensionalizing the Smoluchowski advection-diffusion equation $\partial_t P + v\partial_x P = D\partial_x^2 P$ under rescaling $x \to x/L$ and $t \to vt/L$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: For $\mathrm{Pe} \gg 1$, transport is drift-dominated with narrow arrival-time distributions; for $\mathrm{Pe} \ll 1$, random thermal diffusion dominates and directed ratchet bias is obscured over length $L$.

\\mathrm{Pe}.name: Péclet Number
\\mathrm{Pe}.description: Dimensionless ratio of directed advective transport rate to diffusive transport rate.

v.name: Mean Drift Velocity
v.description: Average directed velocity generated by the ratchet or molecular motor.

L.name: Characteristic Transport Length
L.description: Spatial distance over which directed transport and diffusion are compared.

D.name: Effective Diffusion Coefficient
D.description: Effective longitudinal diffusivity characterizing stochastic dispersion around the mean drift.

formulas.title: Nernst Ionic Reversal Potential
formulas.description: Gives the equilibrium transmembrane reversal potential $E_{\mathrm{ion}}$ at which electrostatic drift exactly cancels diffusive flux for a single permeant ionic species of valence $z$ across a semipermeable biological membrane.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Nernst reversal potential is the exact transmembrane voltage at which the electrochemical potential of an ionic species is equal on both sides of the lipid bilayer, halting net passive ion transport.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A concentration imbalance pushes ions down their gradient until the accumulated electric voltage pushes back with equal strength, locking in a logarithmic equilibrium potential.
formulas.interpretation: Equating intracellular and extracellular electrochemical potentials $\mu_0 + k_B T \ln[\mathrm{ion}]_{\mathrm{in}} + z q V_{\mathrm{in}} = \mu_0 + k_B T \ln[\mathrm{ion}]_{\mathrm{out}} + z q V_{\mathrm{out}}$ directly yields $E_{\mathrm{ion}} = V_{\mathrm{in}} - V_{\mathrm{out}}$. For monovalent ions ($z = +1$) at $310\,\mathrm{K}$, $k_B T / q \approx 26.7\,\mathrm{mV}$, giving a $61.5\,\mathrm{mV}$ shift per decade concentration ratio.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from thermodynamic detailed balance and equilibrium invariance of the electrochemical potential across a semipermeable phase boundary.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Strictly valid for ideal dilute electrolytes permeable to a single ionic species at thermal equilibrium. At high ionic strength, concentrations must be replaced by thermodynamic activities, and multi-ion permeability requires the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz generalization.

E_{\\mathrm{ion}}.name: Nernst Reversal Potential
E_{\\mathrm{ion}}.description: Equilibrium transmembrane voltage (inside minus outside) at which net flux of the ion vanishes.

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Thermal energy conversion constant relating temperature to molecular kinetic energy.

T.name: Absolute Temperature
T.description: Thermodynamic temperature of the aqueous cellular environment.

z.name: Ionic Valence
z.description: Signed integer charge number of the permeant ion (e.g., $+1$ for $\mathrm{Na}^+, \mathrm{K}^+$, $-1$ for $\mathrm{Cl}^-$).

q.name: Elementary Charge
q.description: Magnitude of the proton or electron charge ($1.602 \times 10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$).

[\\mathrm{ion}]_{\\mathrm{out}}.name: Extracellular Ion Concentration
[\\mathrm{ion}]_{\\mathrm{out}}.description: Molar concentration of the ionic species in the extracellular bath.

[\\mathrm{ion}]_{\\mathrm{in}}.name: Intracellular Ion Concentration
[\\mathrm{ion}]_{\\mathrm{in}}.description: Molar concentration of the ionic species in the intracellular cytoplasm.

formulas.title: Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz Resting Membrane Potential Equation
formulas.equation: V_m = \frac{k_B T}{q}\ln\!\left(\frac{P_K [K^+]_o + P_{Na} [Na^+]_o + P_{Cl} [Cl^-]_i}{P_K [K^+]_i + P_{Na} [Na^+]_i + P_{Cl} [Cl^-]_o}\right)
formulas.description: Determines the steady-state resting membrane potential $V_m$ of a cell simultaneously permeable to monovalent potassium ($\mathrm{K}^+$), sodium ($\mathrm{Na}^+$), and chloride ($\mathrm{Cl}^-$) ions weighted by their membrane permeabilities $P_K$, $P_{Na}$, and $P_{Cl}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz voltage equation describes the nonequilibrium steady state in which total net transmembrane electrical current vanishes even though individual ionic species continue to flow down their respective electrochemical gradients.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When a membrane leaks multiple ions at once, the resting voltage settles at a permeability-weighted logarithmic compromise closest to the Nernst potential of the most permeable ion.
formulas.interpretation: Derived by integrating the one-dimensional Nernst-Planck electrodiffusion equation across a homogeneous membrane of uniform electric field and enforcing zero total current $I_K + I_{Na} + I_{Cl} = 0$. Notice that the negatively charged chloride concentrations are inverted relative to the cations.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from steady-state charge conservation across a planar membrane under the constant-field approximation and independent-ion electrodiffusion.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Reduces identically to the Nernst equilibrium potential whenever one ionic permeability dominates the others (e.g., $P_K \gg P_{Na}, P_{Cl}$ gives $V_m \to E_K$). Assumes negligible electrogenic pump current, constant interior electric field, and monovalent ions only.

V_m.name: Resting Membrane Potential
V_m.description: Steady-state transmembrane potential difference (intracellular minus extracellular).

T.name: Absolute Temperature
T.description: Thermodynamic temperature of the membrane system.

P_K.name: Potassium Permeability
P_K.description: Membrane permeability coefficient for potassium ions.

P_{Na}.name: Sodium Permeability
P_{Na}.description: Membrane permeability coefficient for sodium ions.

P_{Cl}.name: Chloride Permeability
P_{Cl}.description: Membrane permeability coefficient for chloride ions.

[K^+]_o.name: Extracellular Potassium Concentration
[K^+]_o.description: External molar concentration of potassium ions.

[K^+]_i.name: Intracellular Potassium Concentration
[K^+]_i.description: Internal molar concentration of potassium ions.

[Na^+]_o.name: Extracellular Sodium Concentration
[Na^+]_o.description: External molar concentration of sodium ions.

[Na^+]_i.name: Intracellular Sodium Concentration
[Na^+]_i.description: Internal molar concentration of sodium ions.

[Cl^-]_i.name: Intracellular Chloride Concentration
[Cl^-]_i.description: Internal molar concentration of chloride ions.

[Cl^-]_o.name: Extracellular Chloride Concentration
[Cl^-]_o.description: External molar concentration of chloride ions.

formulas.title: Hodgkin-Huxley Membrane Current Equation
formulas.equation: C_m \frac{dV}{dt} = I_{\mathrm{ext}} - \bar{g}_{Na} m^3 h (V - E_{Na}) - \bar{g}_K n^4 (V - E_K) - \bar{g}_L (V - E_L)
formulas.description: Governs the time evolution of the transmembrane voltage $V(t)$ in a space-clamped excitable membrane by equating capacitive displacement current $C_m dV/dt$ to external stimulus current $I_{\mathrm{ext}}$ minus nonlinear voltage-gated sodium, potassium, and passive leakage ionic currents.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Hodgkin-Huxley current balance represents the cell membrane as a parallel RC circuit whose nonlinear ionic resistors are dynamically modulated by voltage-dependent channel gating probabilities.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Incoming stimulus current charges the lipid membrane capacitor while competing sodium, potassium, and leak channels drain or inject charge to generate sharp all-or-none action potentials.
formulas.interpretation: Applying Kirchhoff's current law to a unit area of membrane balances capacitive current $C_m dV/dt$ against ohmic ionic branches driven by $(V - E_{\mathrm{ion}})$. Fast activation of $m^3$ creates positive feedback driving depolarization toward $E_{Na}$, while slower inactivation $h$ and potassium activation $n^4$ restore repolarization toward $E_K$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from local electric charge conservation (Kirchhoff's current law) across a parallel equivalent circuit of dielectric capacitance and independent ionic conductance pathways.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for space-clamped isopotential membrane patches with large channel counts where stochastic gating fluctuations average out. Extending to spatially inhomogeneous axons adds a second-order axial diffusion term proportional to $\partial^2 V / \partial x^2$.

C_m.name: Specific Membrane Capacitance
C_m.description: Capacitance per unit area of the phospholipid bilayer (typically $\approx 0.01\,\mathrm{F/m}^2$).

V.name: Transmembrane Voltage
V.description: Instantaneous electrical potential difference across the excitable membrane.

I_{\\mathrm{ext}}.name: External Applied Current Density
I_{\\mathrm{ext}}.description: Injected stimulating or synaptic current per unit membrane area.

\\bar{g}_{Na}.name: Maximal Sodium Conductance
\\bar{g}_{Na}.description: Peak sodium conductance per unit area when all sodium channels are open.

\\bar{g}_K.name: Maximal Potassium Conductance
\\bar{g}_K.description: Peak potassium conductance per unit area when all potassium channels are open.

\\bar{g}_L.name: Leakage Conductance
\\bar{g}_L.description: Voltage-independent passive background conductance per unit area.

m.name: Sodium Activation Gate
m.description: Dimensionless probability that an individual sodium activation subunit is open.

h.name: Sodium Inactivation Gate
h.description: Dimensionless probability that a sodium inactivation subunit is unblocked.

n.name: Potassium Activation Gate
n.description: Dimensionless probability that an individual potassium activation subunit is open.

E_{Na}.name: Sodium Reversal Potential
E_{Na}.description: Nernst equilibrium potential for sodium ions.

E_K.name: Potassium Reversal Potential
E_K.description: Nernst equilibrium potential for potassium ions.

E_L.name: Leakage Reversal Potential
E_L.description: Effective reversal potential of passive background leakage channels.

formulas.title: Voltage-Gated Ion Channel Subunit Kinetics
formulas.description: Describes the first-order kinetic relaxation of a dimensionless voltage-gated channel subunit probability $n(t) \in [0, 1]$ transitioning reversibly between closed and open conformational states with voltage-dependent rates $\alpha_n(V)$ and $\beta_n(V)$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Each gating variable obeys a two-state continuous-time master equation whose forward and backward transition rates reflect thermally activated barrier crossing modulated by the transmembrane electric field.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Channel voltage sensors flip back and forth between closed and open shapes at rates controlled by membrane voltage, relaxing exponentially toward a new equilibrium openness.
formulas.interpretation: Under a voltage clamp at fixed $V$, the equation integrates to exponential relaxation toward $n_\infty(V) = \alpha_n / (\alpha_n + \beta_n)$ with time constant $\tau_n(V) = (\alpha_n + \beta_n)^{-1}$. Identical two-state master equations govern sodium activation $m$ and inactivation $h$ with their respective rate functions.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived from probability conservation ($P_{\mathrm{open}} + P_{\mathrm{closed}} = 1$) and two-state Markov detailed balance in an external electrostatic potential.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid in the mean-field limit of many independent, memoryless two-state subunits. Fails for single-channel patch-clamp recordings where discrete stochastic jumps dominate, or in multi-state channels exhibiting cooperative subunit coupling.

n.name: Gating Subunit Open Probability
n.description: Dimensionless fraction of potassium activation subunits in the permissive open state.

\\alpha_n(V).name: Voltage-Dependent Opening Rate
\\alpha_n(V).description: Transition rate from closed to open subunit conformation as a function of transmembrane voltage $V$.

\\beta_n(V).name: Voltage-Dependent Closing Rate
\\beta_n(V).description: Transition rate from open to closed subunit conformation as a function of transmembrane voltage $V$.

V.name: Transmembrane Voltage
V.description: Membrane potential modulating the conformational free-energy barrier.

formulas.title: One-Dimensional Passive Axonal Cable Equation
formulas.description: Governs the spatiotemporal spread and exponential decay of subthreshold electrotonic potential $V(x, t)$ along a uniform cylindrical passive neurite characterized by membrane time constant $\tau_m$ and length constant $\lambda_m$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The passive cable equation is a leaky diffusion equation expressing current conservation between longitudinal ohmic conduction along the cytoplasm and radial capacitive-resistive loss across the membrane.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Subthreshold electrical signals diffuse along an axon like heat along an uninsulated wire, smearing out in time and fading exponentially with distance as charge leaks through the membrane.
formulas.interpretation: Combining Ohm's law for axial current $I_a = -(\pi a^2 / R_i) \partial V / \partial x$ with radial current conservation $-\partial I_a / \partial x = 2\pi a (C_m \partial V / \partial t + V / R_m)$ yields the dimensionless time- and space-scaled parabolic PDE with $\tau_m = R_m C_m$ and $\lambda_m = \sqrt{a R_m / (2 R_i)}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from local electric charge conservation and cylindrical translational invariance along a uniform passive ohmic fiber.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for small subthreshold perturbations around resting potential where membrane conductance is linear and extracellular resistance is negligible. Breaks down once voltage-gated channels activate or when dendritic branching alters cable diameter.

\\tau_m.name: Membrane Time Constant
\\tau_m.description: Product $R_m C_m$ governing the exponential temporal relaxation of membrane voltage.

\\lambda_m.name: Electrotonic Length Constant
\\lambda_m.description: Characteristic spatial decay length over which steady subthreshold voltage falls by $1/e$.

V.name: Electrotonic Membrane Voltage
V.description: Deviation of transmembrane potential from its resting equilibrium value.

x.name: Axial Position
x.description: Longitudinal spatial coordinate along the cylindrical axon or dendrite.

formulas.title: Axonal Electrotonic Length Constant
formulas.description: Defines the characteristic spatial decay length $\lambda_m$ of a cylindrical passive axon or dendrite of radius $a$, specific membrane resistance $R_m$, and intracellular axial resistivity $R_i$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The electrotonic length constant measures how far passive electrical current travels down the cytoplasmic core before leaking out across the transmembrane resistance.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Wider axons and better-insulated membranes let electrical signals carry further before fading, whereas higher cytoplasmic resistance shortens their reach.
formulas.interpretation: Emerges as the square root of the ratio of radial membrane resistance per unit length $r_m = R_m / (2\pi a)$ to axial cytoplasmic resistance per unit length $r_a = R_i / (\pi a^2)$, giving $\lambda_m = \sqrt{r_m / r_a} = \sqrt{a R_m / (2 R_i)}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Encodes the geometric scaling ratio between cylindrical surface area ($\propto a$) and cross-sectional volume ($\propto a^2$) under axial current conservation.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Assumes a uniform cylindrical cable of constant radius $a$ immersed in a negligible-resistance extracellular bath. In myelinated fibers, high effective $R_m$ dramatically extends $\lambda_m$ across internodal segments.

\\lambda_m.name: Electrotonic Length Constant
\\lambda_m.description: Distance over which a steady-state passive potential drops to $1/e$ of its initial amplitude.

a.name: Axon Radius
a.description: Inner radius of the cylindrical cytoplasmic core.

R_m.name: Specific Membrane Resistance
R_m.description: Transmembrane electrical resistance multiplied by unit membrane area.

R_i.name: Intracellular Axial Resistivity
R_i.description: Bulk electrical resistivity of the conducting axoplasm.

formulas.title: Unmyelinated Axon Action Potential Conduction Velocity Scaling
formulas.description: Establishes how the propagation speed $v_{\mathrm{AP}}$ of a regenerative action potential along an unmyelinated cylindrical axon scales with fiber radius $a$, intracellular axial resistivity $R_i$, and specific membrane capacitance $C_m$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Conduction velocity along an active unmyelinated cable scales as the ratio of electrotonic spread to local capacitive charging time, producing a square-root dependence on axon radius.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Doubling an unmyelinated nerve's conduction speed requires quadrupling its radius, explaining why invertebrates evolved giant axons while vertebrates invented insulating myelin.
formulas.interpretation: Substituting the traveling-wave ansatz $V(x - v_{\mathrm{AP}} t)$ into the active Hodgkin-Huxley cable equation yields a dimensionless eigenvalue $K$ linking active conductance to wave speed via $v_{\mathrm{AP}} = \sqrt{a / (2 R_i C_m^2 R_{\mathrm{act}})} \cdot K \propto \sqrt{a / (R_i C_m^2)}$ when channel densities are fixed.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from dimensional scaling invariance of the nonlinear reaction-diffusion cable equation under traveling-wave coordinates.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for uniform unmyelinated axons with constant intrinsic ion-channel kinetics and density. In myelinated vertebrate axons, saltatory conduction between nodes of Ranvier changes the scaling to linear in fiber diameter ($v_{\mathrm{AP}} \propto a$).

v_{\\mathrm{AP}}.name: Action Potential Conduction Velocity
v_{\\mathrm{AP}}.description: Steady propagation speed of the regenerative nerve impulse along the axon.

a.name: Axon Radius
a.description: Inner radius of the cylindrical unmyelinated fiber.

R_i.name: Intracellular Axial Resistivity
R_i.description: Specific electrical resistivity of the intracellular axoplasm.

C_m.name: Specific Membrane Capacitance
C_m.description: Capacitance per unit surface area of the excitable lipid bilayer.

formulas.title: Helfrich Curvature Elastic Free Energy
formulas.description: Expresses the curvature elastic free energy $F_{\mathrm{bend}}$ of a fluid amphiphilic bilayer as a surface integral over mean curvature $H$, spontaneous curvature $c_0$, and Gaussian curvature $K$, weighted by the bending rigidity $\kappa$ and Gaussian saddle-splay modulus $\bar{\kappa}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Helfrich Hamiltonian is the lowest-order rotationally and translationally invariant elastic free energy functional describing out-of-plane bending of an incompressible two-dimensional fluid membrane.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Bending a fluid lipid sheet away from its preferred spontaneous curvature costs energy proportional to the squared mean curvature, plus a saddle-splay term sensitive to surface topology.
formulas.interpretation: Constructed by expanding the local free energy per unit area to quadratic order in the two principal curvatures $c_1$ and $c_2$ using the two Euclidean invariants $2H = c_1 + c_2$ and $K = c_1 c_2$. Setting $c_0 = 0$ recovers the symmetric Canham bending functional.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Dictated by three-dimensional Euclidean rotational and translational invariance combined with two-dimensional in-plane fluidity (reparameterization invariance and zero shear modulus).
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid when the bilayer thickness $h_0 \approx 4\,\mathrm{nm}$ is much smaller than the local radii of curvature ($|H| h_0 \ll 1$) and area stretching is negligible compared to bending.

F_{\\mathrm{bend}}.name: Bending Free Energy
F_{\\mathrm{bend}}.description: Total elastic curvature free energy stored in the deformed membrane.

\\kappa.name: Bending Rigidity
\\kappa.description: Mean-curvature elastic modulus quantifying resistance to bending, typically $10$–$30\,k_B T$ for phospholipid bilayers.

H.name: Mean Curvature
H.description: Arithmetic mean $(c_1 + c_2)/2$ of the two local principal curvatures of the surface.

c_0.name: Spontaneous Curvature
c_0.description: Preferred intrinsic curvature induced by compositional or environmental asymmetry between the two bilayer leaflets.

\\bar{\\kappa}.name: Gaussian Curvature Modulus
\\bar{\\kappa}.description: Saddle-splay elastic modulus governing the energetic cost of Gaussian curvature and topological changes.

K.name: Gaussian Curvature
K.description: Product $c_1 c_2$ of the two local principal curvatures.

dA.name: Surface Area Element
dA.description: Infinitesimal differential area patch on the curved two-dimensional manifold.

formulas.title: Gauss-Bonnet Topological Curvature Integral
formulas.description: States that the integral of the Gaussian curvature $K = c_1 c_2$ over any closed, smooth, orientable two-dimensional membrane surface equals $4\pi(1 - g)$, where $g$ is the topological genus (number of handles).
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Gauss-Bonnet invariant links local differential surface geometry to global membrane topology, proving that the saddle-splay energy is invariant under continuous shape deformations that preserve genus.
formulas.intuitive_summary: No matter how you dent or stretch a closed vesicle without tearing or fusing it, its total integrated Gaussian curvature stays locked to its number of handles.
formulas.interpretation: In the Helfrich bending functional, $\bar{\kappa}\int K\,dA = 4\pi\bar{\kappa}(1 - g)$ contributes a constant offset for fixed topology ($g = 0$ for a sphere, $g = 1$ for a torus) and only changes during fusion, fission, or pore formation.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from differential topological invariance (diffeomorphism invariance of the Euler characteristic $\chi = 2 - 2g$) of compact two-dimensional manifolds without boundary.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Applies to closed, boundaryless, orientable $C^2$ surfaces. For open membranes with an exposed edge $\partial M$, an additional geodesic curvature boundary integral $\oint_{\partial M} k_g\,ds$ must be included.

K.name: Gaussian Curvature
K.description: Intrinsic curvature defined as the product $c_1 c_2$ of local principal curvatures.

dA.name: Surface Area Element
dA.description: Infinitesimal area element integrated over the closed membrane surface.

g.name: Topological Genus
g.description: Non-negative integer counting the number of handles or holes of the closed orientable surface ($g = 0$ sphere, $g = 1$ torus).

formulas.title: Monge-Gauge Quadratic Membrane Fluctuation Hamiltonian
formulas.description: Gives the quadratic effective free energy $F_{\mathrm{Monge}}$ of a nearly planar fluid membrane with height profile $h(\mathbf{r})$, lateral surface tension $\sigma$, and bending rigidity $\kappa$ in the small-gradient Monge representation.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Linearizing the Helfrich bending energy and area-tension work for small out-of-plane slopes yields a Gaussian field theory balancing capillary surface tension against fourth-order curvature elasticity.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Small ripples on a nearly flat membrane cost energy in two ways: stretching the sheet against lateral tension and curving it against its bending stiffness.
formulas.interpretation:
Obtained by expanding $dA = \sqrt{1 + |
abla h|^2}\,d^2r \approx (1 +  rac{1}{2}|
abla h|^2)\,d^2r$ and $2H \approx 
abla^2 h$ to quadratic order in $h(\mathbf{r})$ for a symmetric bilayer ($c_0 = 0$) of fixed topology.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Inherits two-dimensional translational and rotational invariance in the reference plane as well as height-translation symmetry $h(\mathbf{r}) \to h(\mathbf{r}) + \text{const}$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid only for overhang-free single-valued height fields with small slopes ($|\nabla h| \ll 1$) and symmetric leaflets ($c_0 = 0$); breaks down near the persistence length where thermal crumpling induces large gradients.

F_{\\mathrm{Monge}}.name: Monge-Gauge Fluctuation Free Energy
F_{\\mathrm{Monge}}.description: Excess quadratic elastic and capillary energy relative to a flat reference plane.

\\sigma.name: Surface Tension
\\sigma.description: Effective lateral tension conjugated to the excess membrane area.

h.name: Membrane Height Field
h.description: Normal vertical displacement of the bilayer midplane above the reference $(x, y)$ plane.

\\kappa.name: Bending Rigidity
\\kappa.description: Bending modulus penalizing mean curvature squared.

d^2r.name: Projected Area Element
d^2r.description: Infinitesimal area element $dx\,dy$ in the flat base plane.

formulas.title: Thermal Membrane Undulation Power Spectrum
formulas.description: Gives the equilibrium mean-square Fourier amplitude $\langle |h(\mathbf{q})|^2 \rangle$ of thermal height undulations at in-plane wavevector $\mathbf{q}$ for a membrane of projected area $A$, tension $\sigma$, and bending rigidity $\kappa$ at temperature $T$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: By the equipartition theorem applied to each independent Fourier mode of the Monge Hamiltonian, thermal energy $k_B T$ excites long-wavelength capillary modes as $q^{-2}$ and short-wavelength bending modes as $q^{-4}$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Heat makes a lipid sheet shimmer with ripples whose intensity falls off as $1/q^2$ at large scales controlled by tension and steeply as $1/q^4$ at small scales controlled by bending stiffness.
formulas.interpretation: Substituting the Fourier expansion $h(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{\mathbf{q}} h(\mathbf{q}) e^{i\mathbf{q}\cdot\mathbf{r}}$ into $F_{\mathrm{Monge}}$ diagonalizes the energy as $\frac{A}{2}\sum_{\mathbf{q}} (\sigma q^2 + \kappa q^4)|h(\mathbf{q})|^2$, so equipartition sets each mode's average energy to $\frac{1}{2}k_B T$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from planar translational invariance (diagonalizing the quadratic form in Fourier space) and thermal equilibrium invariance under canonical Boltzmann weighting.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Holds for wavevectors $2\pi/\sqrt{A} \lesssim q \lesssim 2\pi/a$ within the small-slope Gaussian regime ($|\nabla h| \ll 1$). The tension-to-bending crossover occurs at $q_c = \sqrt{\sigma/\kappa}$.

h(\\mathbf{q}).name: Fourier Height Amplitude
h(\\mathbf{q}).description: In-plane Fourier component of the vertical membrane displacement at wavevector $\mathbf{q}$.

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Fundamental constant converting absolute temperature into thermal energy.

T.name: Absolute Temperature
T.description: Thermodynamic temperature of the aqueous bath.

A.name: Projected Membrane Area
A.description: Area of the flat base plane over which the Fourier decomposition is defined.

\\sigma.name: Surface Tension
\\sigma.description: Lateral mechanical tension acting on the bilayer.

\\kappa.name: Bending Rigidity
\\kappa.description: Helfrich bending modulus resisting curvature fluctuations.

q.name: In-Plane Wavevector Magnitude

formulas.title: Helfrich Entropic Steric Repulsion Pressure
formulas.description: Quantifies the long-range entropic disjoining pressure $P_{\mathrm{steric}}(d)$ pushing apart stacked fluid membranes at mean separation $d$ due to steric confinement of thermal bending undulations.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Restricting a thermally fluctuating bilayer between neighboring walls suppresses its long-wavelength undulation modes, lowering configurational entropy and generating a repulsive pressure scaling as $(k_B T)^2 / (\kappa d^3)$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Squeezing wiggling lipid sheets closer together cramps their thermal undulations, creating an entropic pushback that grows stronger as the inverse cube of the gap.
formulas.interpretation: Each collision patch of lateral area $\xi_\parallel^2 \sim (\kappa / k_B T) d^2$ loses roughly $k_B T$ of configurational free energy, giving confinement free energy per area $\Delta f = c_H (k_B T)^2 / (\kappa d^2)$ with Helfrich's self-consistent prefactor $c_H = 3\pi^2 / 128$; differentiating $-\partial \Delta f / \partial d$ yields the $3\pi^2 / 64$ coefficient.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Emerges from scale invariance of the tensionless bending Hamiltonian ($\sigma = 0$) combined with hard-wall steric non-interpenetration between adjacent bilayers.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for tensionless fluid bilayers ($\sigma d^2 \ll \kappa$) at separations $d$ much larger than the bilayer thickness $h_0$ and hydration decay length ($\sim 0.2\,\mathrm{nm}$). Strong lateral tension exponentially suppresses the repulsion.

P_{\\mathrm{steric}}.name: Entropic Steric Repulsion Pressure
P_{\\mathrm{steric}}.description: Repulsive disjoining force per unit area between neighboring confined fluid membranes.

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Constant relating thermal energy to absolute temperature.

T.name: Absolute Temperature
T.description: Equilibrium temperature of the multilamellar suspension.

\\kappa.name: Bending Rigidity
\\kappa.description: Bare curvature elasticity modulus of an individual bilayer.

d.name: Mean Intermembrane Separation
d.description: Average water-layer spacing between adjacent parallel bilayers.

formulas.title: Scale-Dependent Bending Rigidity Renormalization
formulas.description: Describes the logarithmic thermal softening of the effective bending rigidity $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}(L)$ of a tensionless fluid membrane observed on length scale $L$ relative to its bare microscopic rigidity $\kappa$ at molecular cutoff $a$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: One-loop renormalization group integration over nonlinear geometric couplings among short-wavelength undulations reduces the macroscopic bending stiffness of a fluid sheet as observation scale grows.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A fluid lipid sheet looks floppier when viewed on larger scales because tiny thermal ripples store excess area that makes large-scale bending easier.
formulas.interpretation: Derived by Peliti and Leibler (1985) via momentum-shell integration of quartic curvature and metric nonlinearities in the Helfrich functional; vanishing of $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}(\xi_p) = 0$ defines the de Gennes-Taupin persistence length $\xi_p = a \exp[4\pi\kappa / (3 k_B T)]$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Protected by rotational invariance in three-dimensional embedding space and two-dimensional reparameterization invariance of fluid surfaces lacking in-plane shear rigidity.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid in the weak-coupling perturbative regime $k_B T / (4\pi\kappa) \ll 1$ and for scales $a \ll L \ll \xi_p$. Breaks down near $L \sim \xi_p$ where the membrane enters a thermally crumpled phase.

\\kappa_{\\mathrm{eff}}.name: Effective Bending Rigidity
\\kappa_{\\mathrm{eff}}.description: Scale-dependent renormalized bending modulus measured at length scale $L$.

\\kappa.name: Bare Bending Rigidity
\\kappa.description: Microscopic bending modulus defined at the molecular cutoff length $a$.

L.name: Observation Length Scale
L.description: Coarse-graining or lateral membrane length scale ($L > a$).

a.name: Molecular Cutoff Length
a.description: Short-distance ultraviolet cutoff comparable to lipid headgroup spacing or bilayer thickness.

formulas.title: Cylindrical Membrane Tether Pulling Force
formulas.description: Gives the equilibrium axial force $f_{\mathrm{tether}}$ required to hold or quasi-statically pull a narrow cylindrical lipid nanotube from a fluid vesicle of bending rigidity $\kappa$ and lateral surface tension $\sigma$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Balancing curvature energy against lateral tension in a cylindrical membrane tube fixes both its equilibrium radius $R_0 = \sqrt{\kappa/(2\sigma)}$ and a constant length-independent pulling force proportional to $\sqrt{\kappa\sigma}$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Pulling a thin tube out of a tense lipid vesicle takes a steady force set by the geometric mean of bending stiffness and membrane tension, regardless of how long the tube grows.
formulas.interpretation: For a cylinder of radius $R$ and length $L_t$ with $2H = 1/R$ and $K = 0$, the total energy $F = 2\pi R L_t [\kappa/(2R^2) + \sigma] - f_{\mathrm{tether}} L_t$ is stationary with respect to $R$ at $R_0 = \sqrt{\kappa/(2\sigma)}$ and with respect to $L_t$ at $f_{\mathrm{tether}} = 2\pi\sqrt{2\kappa\sigma}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from axial translational invariance along the cylindrical nanotube and variational minimization of the Helfrich plus surface-tension free energy.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for symmetric bilayers ($c_0 = 0$) in quasi-static equilibrium when the tether length $L_t \gg R_0$ and membrane area reservoir is large enough that $\sigma$ stays constant; nonzero $c_0$ shifts the force to $2\pi(\sqrt{2\kappa\sigma} - \kappa c_0)$.

f_{\\mathrm{tether}}.name: Tether Pulling Force
f_{\\mathrm{tether}}.description: Equilibrium axial force required to maintain a cylindrical membrane nanotube.

\\kappa.name: Bending Rigidity
\\kappa.description: Helfrich bending modulus resisting the tight radial curvature of the tube.

\\sigma.name: Lateral Surface Tension
\\sigma.description: Effective membrane tension in the parent vesicle reservoir.

formulas.title: Random Energy Model Gaussian Density of States
formulas.description: Gives the number of accessible conformational microstates $\Omega(E)$ at energy $E$ in Derrida's Random Energy Model as a Gaussian centered at the mean non-native energy $\bar{E}$ with energetic variance $\Delta E^2$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: When a heteropolymer's total energy sums many weakly correlated, competing monomer-monomer interactions, the central limit theorem distributes its compact non-native configurational energies normally around $\bar{E}$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Most random compact shapes of a polymer cluster near an average energy, while exponentially fewer conformations reach the extreme low-energy tail.
formulas.interpretation: Taking the microcanonical entropy $S(E) = k_B \ln \Omega(E) = k_B \ln \Omega_0 - k_B (E - \bar{E})^2 / (2\Delta E^2)$ reveals a parabolic entropy profile that vanishes at the glass ground-state energy $E_g = \bar{E} - \Delta E \sqrt{2 \ln \Omega_0}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from statistical independence of microstate energies and the central limit theorem applied to a large sum of quenched random pair interactions.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid for energies above the discrete lower edge $E_g$ where $\Omega(E) \ge 1$; below $E_g$ the continuum Gaussian predicts fewer than one state and must be truncated by extreme-value statistics.

\\Omega(E).name: Conformational Density of States
\\Omega(E).description: Number of distinct compact heteropolymer microstates at energy $E$.

\\Omega_0.name: Total Compact Conformational Multiplicity
\\Omega_0.description: Total number of compact non-native configurations scaling exponentially with chain length $N$.

E.name: Conformational Energy
E.description: Total interaction energy of a given compact polypeptide configuration.

\\bar{E}.name: Mean Non-Native Energy
\\bar{E}.description: Average energy across the ensemble of compact random conformations.

\\Delta E.name: Energy Landscape Ruggedness
\\Delta E.description: Standard deviation of non-native configurational energies quantifying energetic disorder.

formulas.title: Random Energy Model Glass Transition Temperature
formulas.description: Determines the thermodynamic glass transition temperature $T_g$ below which a disordered heteropolymer in the Random Energy Model freezes into its lowest non-native energy traps.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The glass temperature marks the entropy crisis where the canonical ensemble exhausts the continuous band of random conformations and condenses onto a few structurally unrelated low-energy minima.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Greater energetic ruggedness $\Delta E$ raises the freezing temperature, whereas a larger conformational entropy $\ln \Omega_0$ helps keep the chain fluid down to lower temperatures.
formulas.interpretation: Obtained by equating the thermodynamic temperature $1/T = \partial S / \partial E = -(E - \bar{E})/(k_B \Delta E^2)$ at the zero-entropy threshold $E_g = \bar{E} - \Delta E \sqrt{2 \ln \Omega_0}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from the breakdown of replica symmetry and vanishing configurational entropy in the thermodynamic limit of the Random Energy Model.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Applicable for large $\ln \Omega_0 \gg 1$ (long chains); for finite-length proteins, kinetic slowing sets in smoothly near $T_g$ rather than as a sharp singularity.

T_g.name: Glass Transition Temperature
T_g.description: Temperature at which configurational entropy vanishes and glassy trapping dominates.

\\Delta E.name: Energy Landscape Ruggedness
\\Delta E.description: Standard deviation of non-native conformational energies.

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Fundamental proportionality constant linking thermal energy to absolute temperature.

\\Omega_0.name: Total Compact Conformational Multiplicity
\\Omega_0.description: Total number of compact non-native conformations.

formulas.title: Minimal-Frustration Foldability Ratio
formulas.description: Expresses the dimensionless ratio of the thermodynamic folding temperature $T_f$ to the glass transition temperature $T_g$ in terms of the native energy gap $\delta E_{\mathrm{gap}}$, landscape ruggedness $\Delta E$, and conformational entropy $\ln \Omega_0$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Bryngelson-Wolynes foldability criterion quantifies how strongly the funnel slope toward the native state dominates over non-native energetic traps.
formulas.intuitive_summary: A protein folds rapidly and reliably only when its native state sits far enough below the rugged sea of misfolded shapes that folding occurs well above the glassy freezing point.
formulas.interpretation: Equating native energy $E_N = \bar{E} - \delta E_{\mathrm{gap}}$ to the random-state free energy gives $T_f \approx \delta E_{\mathrm{gap}} / (k_B \ln \Omega_0)$ in the large-gap limit; dividing by $T_g = \Delta E / (k_B \sqrt{2 \ln \Omega_0})$ yields $T_f / T_g$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Emerges from comparing the evolutionary symmetry-breaking native bias $\delta E_{\mathrm{gap}}$ against the statistically symmetric Gaussian disorder width $\Delta E$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid when $T_f > T_g$ (minimally frustrated funnel regime); as $T_f / T_g \to 1$, kinetic traps slow folding exponentially and the sequence becomes an unfolder or glass former.

T_f.name: Folding Transition Temperature
T_f.description: Temperature at which native and unfolded ensembles have equal free energy.

T_g.name: Glass Transition Temperature
T_g.description: Temperature below which glassy non-native traps arrest conformational diffusion.

\\delta E_{\\mathrm{gap}}.name: Native Stability Energy Gap
\\delta E_{\\mathrm{gap}}.description: Energy separation $\bar{E} - E_N$ between the mean non-native ensemble and the native structure.

\\Delta E.name: Energy Landscape Ruggedness
\\Delta E.description: Standard deviation of non-native decoy energies.

formulas.title: Gibbs-Helmholtz Protein Folding Stability Curve
formulas.description: Gives the temperature-dependent unfolding Gibbs free energy $\Delta G(T) = G_U(T) - G_N(T)$ of a two-state protein in terms of its melting temperature $T_m$, unfolding enthalpy $\Delta H_m$, and constant-pressure heat capacity change $\Delta C_p$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Incorporating the positive heat capacity increment $\Delta C_p$ from hydrophobic hydration bends the linear van't Hoff stability line into a concave curve exhibiting both thermal and cold denaturation.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Because unfolding exposes oily core residues that order surrounding water, protein stability peaks at an intermediate temperature and falls off if the solution gets either too hot or too cold.
formulas.interpretation: Obtained by integrating $\Delta H(T) = \Delta H_m + \Delta C_p(T - T_m)$ and $\Delta S(T) = \Delta H_m/T_m + \Delta C_p \ln(T/T_m)$ into $\Delta G(T) = \Delta H(T) - T\Delta S(T)$ with $\Delta G(T_m) = 0$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows from the fundamental thermodynamic identities $\partial \Delta H / \partial T = \Delta C_p$ and $\partial \Delta S / \partial T = \Delta C_p / T$ at constant pressure.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Assumes temperature-independent $\Delta C_p$ over the physiological range and strictly reversible two-state equilibrium; breaks down if aggregation occurs or $\Delta C_p(T)$ varies strongly at extreme temperatures.

\\Delta G(T).name: Folding Free Energy Change
\\Delta G(T).description: Gibbs free energy difference $G_U - G_N$ (or $G_N - G_U$ by convention) governing thermodynamic stability at temperature $T$.

\\Delta H_m.name: Unfolding Enthalpy at Midpoint
\\Delta H_m.description: Enthalpy change of the folding transition evaluated at $T = T_m$.

T.name: Absolute Temperature
T.description: Thermodynamic temperature of the aqueous protein solution.

T_m.name: Thermal Melting Temperature
T_m.description: Midpoint temperature at which $\Delta G(T_m) = 0$ and folded and unfolded states are equally populated.

\\Delta C_p.name: Unfolding Heat Capacity Change
\\Delta C_p.description: Constant-pressure heat capacity increment upon unfolding, dominated by apolar hydration.

formulas.title: Kramers Diffusive Protein Folding Rate
formulas.description: Expresses the first-order protein folding rate constant $k_f$ over a free-energy barrier $\Delta F^\ddagger$ along the native-contact reaction coordinate in terms of the diffusive prefactor $k_0$ and thermal energy $k_B T$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Unlike gas-phase bond breaking, polypeptide folding is an overdamped diffusive escape over an entropic-enthalpic free-energy saddle point, setting a microsecond speed limit $k_0$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Folding speed drops exponentially with the height of the free-energy barrier, while the prefactor $k_0$ captures how fast the chain can reconfigure through viscous water.
formulas.interpretation: Derived from Kramers' Fokker-Planck escape-rate theory in the high-friction regime via saddle-point integration across the barrier top, where $k_0 = D_Q \omega_u \omega_\ddagger / (2\pi k_B T)$ scales with configurational diffusivity $D_Q$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Consequence of detailed balance and local thermal equilibrium in the reactant well prior to diffusive barrier crossing.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid when $\Delta F^\ddagger \gg k_B T$ so barrier crossing is rate-limiting; when $\Delta F^\ddagger \lesssim k_B T$, folding enters the barrierless downhill regime governed directly by $k_0$.

k_f.name: Folding Rate Constant
k_f.description: First-order kinetic rate of transition from the unfolded ensemble to the native basin.

k_0.name: Diffusive Kinetic Prefactor
k_0.description: Barrierless folding speed limit (~$10^6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$) set by chain friction and solvent viscosity.

\\Delta F^\\ddagger.name: Folding Activation Free Energy Barrier
\\Delta F^\\ddagger.description: Height of the transition-state free-energy saddle relative to the unfolded well.

T.name: Absolute Temperature
T.description: Absolute temperature of the folding medium.

formulas.title: Linear Denaturant Stability Relation
formulas.description: Relates the folding free energy $\Delta G([D])$ at chemical denaturant concentration $[D]$ linearly to the native stability in pure water $\Delta G_{\mathrm{H_2O}}$ through the denaturant sensitivity slope $m$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Cosolvents such as urea and guanidinium chloride lower the free energy of unfolded conformations in proportion to the newly exposed backbone and side-chain surface area.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Each increment of added denaturant chips away a fixed amount of native stability, letting experimenters extrapolate straight back to zero denaturant to measure stability in water.
formulas.interpretation: Follows from the linear extrapolation model (LEM) where preferential cosolvent binding shifts chemical potentials proportionally to solvent-accessible surface area change $\Delta \mathrm{ASA}$, giving $m \propto \Delta \mathrm{ASA}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Reflects first-order linear response of the solvation free energy to weak non-specific cosolvent-polypeptide interactions.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Holds accurately across the transition zone of two-state proteins in urea or guanidinium chloride; curvature in chevron arms indicates transition-state movement (Hammond effect) or populated folding intermediates.

\\Delta G([D]).name: Denaturant-Dependent Folding Free Energy
\\Delta G([D]).description: Thermodynamic stability of the native state at denaturant concentration $[D]$.

\\Delta G_{\\mathrm{H_2O}}.name: Native Stability in Pure Water
\\Delta G_{\\mathrm{H_2O}}.description: Extrapolated folding free energy at zero denaturant concentration.

m.name: Denaturant m-Value
m.description: Linear sensitivity coefficient proportional to the solvent-accessible surface area buried upon folding.

[D].name: Denaturant Molar Concentration
[D].description: Molar concentration of chemical denaturant (e.g., urea or guanidinium chloride).

formulas.title: Two-State Equilibrium Folded Fraction
formulas.description: Gives the equilibrium fraction $f_N(T)$ of polypeptide chains occupying the native state in a cooperative two-state folding transition governed by the free energy difference $\Delta G(T) = G_N(T) - G_U(T)$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: When folding intermediates are negligibly populated, the canonical partition function reduces to two macroscopic basins whose relative occupancy follows a logistic Boltzmann curve.
formulas.intuitive_summary: The folded fraction switches sharply from nearly one to nearly zero across the melting temperature as the stability gap changes sign relative to thermal energy $k_B T$.
formulas.interpretation: Follows directly from the two-state canonical partition function $Z = Z_N + Z_U$ with $f_N = Z_N / (Z_N + Z_U) = [1 + \exp(\Delta G / k_B T)]^{-1}$, passing through $f_N = 1/2$ at $\Delta G(T_m) = 0$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Consequence of canonical equilibrium probability normalization over a two-basin free-energy manifold.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Strictly valid for all-or-none cooperative two-state folders; multi-domain proteins or chains with stable intermediates require a multi-state partition sum.

f_N(T).name: Equilibrium Folded Fraction
f_N(T).description: Dimensionless probability that a protein molecule occupies the native basin at temperature $T$.

\\Delta G(T).name: Native-Minus-Unfolded Free Energy
\\Delta G(T).description: Gibbs free energy difference $G_N(T) - G_U(T)$ (negative when the native state is favored).

k_B.name: Boltzmann Constant
k_B.description: Boltzmann constant converting temperature to energy.
